title: tooling(pin): keep one pinned @objectstack build per machine and copy it into each new checkout (objectui#12972)
body:
Fixes #12972
Clause-②: no

A build of the pinned `@objectstack/*` is now kept **once per machine**, outside every checkout, and a fresh worktree **copies** it instead of rebuilding it. Measured here: a second fresh worktree's `pnpm run setup` goes from 192.4 s to 8.7 s. Only `scripts/objectstack-pin.mjs`, its test, and one paragraph in `CONTRIBUTING.md` change.

## How it works (`scripts/objectstack-pin.mjs`, header section "One build per machine")

- **Store:** `$OBJECTSTACK_PIN_STORE`. If that is unset, `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/objectstack-pin`, and otherwise `~/.cache/objectstack-pin` (`storeDir`). In this container that is `/root/.cache/objectstack-pin`.
- **Entry name:** `PIN-HASH` (`storeKey`). HASH is the first 16 hex characters of a sha256 over the script's own bytes. These are the same two inputs CI's cache key hashes, so an entry built by an older script is never reused.
- **Reuse (`takeFromStore`):** when a checkout's cache is not the pin, the entry is copied into the usual staging directory. The **copy** is then checked: the cache's own stamp check (`judgeStamp`: pin, recipe, package set, manifests) plus the content hash recorded at publish. Only after that is it linked beside the committed manifests and renamed into `node_modules/.cache/objectstack`. If any check fails, the copy is discarded, the reason is printed, and the pin is built.
- **Publish (`publishToStore`):** only a build this run made is published. A cache judged current is never published, because its bytes may have been written to since it was built. Publishing is: copy into a `.tmp-` directory in the store, hash it, then rename it into place. A reader therefore finds either no entry or a whole one. When a concurrent run renamed first, the second run drops its copy. A failed publish only prints a warning.
- **Eviction (`pruneStore`):** the store keeps the current entry and the most recently used others, `STORE_KEEP` = 4 in all (a reuse touches the entry's mtime). It also removes temporary directories more than an hour old, which a killed run left behind.
- **Stand-ins:** an `OBJECTSTACK_ROOT` stand-in is not the pin, so it never computes an entry and never reads or writes the store.
- **Status:** `pnpm objectstack:status` prints the entry path and whether it exists.

## Copy, hardlink or symlink: copy

Measured on the real 201 MB / 2182-file cache in this container:

- copy (`fs.cpSync`): 0.50 s, +201 MB
- hardlink (`cp -al`): 0.05 s, +0.35 MB
- symlink: 0 s, 0 MB
- content check on reuse (`hashTree`): 0.81 s

Assessed on the four axes:

- **Real business need:** the measured cost is time, about 180 s per dispatch. A copy recovers 95% of it. A hardlink would also save about 201 MB per worktree. With at most three devs per container and about 25 GB free, disk is not the binding constraint.
- **Long-term soundness:** within a checkout the cache is already hard-linked into `.objectstack-pin` and from there into `node_modules`. A linked entry would turn one checkout's write into a machine-wide write. Read-only mode does not stop that here, because this container runs as root and root ignores permission bits.
- **Preventing AI mistakes:** the fleet has a recorded case of a dev probe appending a marker line to a linked `dist/index.mjs`. With links, that becomes silent corruption of every other agent's worktree and of the entry itself. A copy makes this impossible, and a test pins it: a marker appended in one checkout never reaches the entry.
- **No scope creep at this stage:** a copy is one `fs.cpSync`, with no permission management. A symlink is ruled out by card item 4 alone: `actions/cache` would save the link, not the build.

How the shared entry is protected:

1. Nothing ever links to it; copies are made in both directions.
2. Only a fresh build is ever published.
3. Every reuse checks the copy (stamp, then content hash) before using it.

## Card item 3: the measurement (`pnpm run setup`, two fresh worktrees in a row, then concurrent pairs)

Disk is `du -sk` over the pnpm store, the worktree and the pin store in a single invocation. The pnpm store is listed first, so hardlinks shared with it are not charged to the worktree. All runs were under the container's verify lock, with one other os-dev active, so absolute seconds are shared-box readings; the ratios hold.

| case | time | disk unique to the worktree | pin store |
|---|---|---|---|
| card: a fresh worktree, cold (layout before objectui#13008) | 175.7 s | +295 MB | n/a |
| card: the first worktree's cache copied in | 6.5 s | +286 MB | n/a |
| base `b014f5e`, cold, this container, today | 189.8 s | +286 MB (cache 201 MB) | n/a |
| this PR: first fresh worktree, cold, empty store | 192.4 s | +286 MB | +201 MB, once per pin and script |
| this PR: second fresh worktree right after (warm) | **8.7 s** | +286 MB (its own 201 MB copy) | +0 |
| this PR: two fresh worktrees at once, warm | 11.4 s and 11.4 s | +286 MB each | +0 |
| this PR: two fresh worktrees at once, cold, empty store | 222.0 s and 224.8 s | +286 MB each | +201 MB: one run "published for every checkout on this machine", the other "another run published it first"; no temporary directory left |

The warm run took 8.7 s against 192.4 s cold, about 95% less. Publishing adds roughly a copy plus a hash (about 1.3 s by the measurements above) to a cold build. A hardlinked warm worktree would be about +85 MB (286 − 201). That figure is derived from the measured parts, not a measured full run.

## Card items

1. **Done.** The build is kept once per machine, outside every checkout's `node_modules`, keyed by `.objectstack-sha` and the bytes of `scripts/objectstack-pin.mjs`. The path is documented in the script header and in `CONTRIBUTING.md`, and `OBJECTSTACK_PIN_STORE` overrides it.
2. **Done, by copy.** Both reused worktrees ran `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` with exit 0. objectui#12957's lockfile check (`assertLockfileRecordsBuild`) passed on the reuse path. `git status` was empty afterwards, and `@objectstack/spec` imports. A mismatched or partial entry is never reused; five test cases cover this: another pin, a missing package, a missing file, one changed byte, and a missing record.
3. **Done:** the table above.
4. **Held.** No file under `.github/` changed. `node_modules/.cache/objectstack` is still the directory CI saves and restores, and still the one whose stamp turbo hashes. A CI cache hit takes the skip branch and never reaches the store. On a cache miss the runner publishes once into its own home directory; that is not the CI cache and nothing reads it there. The resolution form is untouched: `git diff b014f5e HEAD -- package.json pnpm-lock.yaml .objectstack-pin .github` is empty.

## The PM's mechanism hypotheses, measured

1. **Confirmed at `b014f5e`:**
   - `CACHE_DIR` is `node_modules/.cache/objectstack`.
   - `materialize(root, overrides, { from, mode, replaced })` takes its source directory as an argument.
   - `linkTree` falls back to a copy when a link fails.
   - The skip branch still calls `materialize`.
   - Cold setup re-measured: 189.8 s, +286 MB.
2. **Atomic publish, measured as a concurrent pair:**
   - In the cold pair both runs built, one rename won, and the other dropped its copy.
   - There is deliberately no lock. A lock would save one build only when two worktrees start cold on the same pin at the same moment, and handling stale locks is not worth that.
   - A reader racing a prune sees the failure as a failed stamp or hash check on its copy.
3. **Copy, as argued above.**
4. **The key is the pin plus the script hash.**
   - The override set is not part of the key. An entry built for another package set fails the stamp check and is rebuilt, never reused. CI's key has the same shape.
   - Stand-in builds neither read nor write the store; a test and an ablation pin this.
5. **The default is under the user cache directory, overridden by `OBJECTSTACK_PIN_STORE`.** It works in this container and on Linux and macOS laptops.

## Tests and ablations

- In `scripts/__tests__/objectstack-pin.test.ts`, a new describe block, "one build per machine, outside every checkout", adds nine tests:
  - the documented, overridable path and the key;
  - publish once, then a copy reused through `build()` at the pin, offline;
  - five spoiled entries, each refused with its reason, staging emptied, and a fall-back to building;
  - the lost rename race;
  - eviction.
- The stand-in test now also asserts that the store was never created.
- The whole file stubs `OBJECTSTACK_PIN_STORE`, so no build in it can reach a developer's real store.
- Five one-behaviour ablations, each through `ablation-replace.mjs` with the mutation verified on disk and the restore proved (blob equals HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty). Each one failed:

| ablation | failed |
|---|---|
| hash check on reuse removed | "a file gone", "a byte changed" |
| reuse copy replaced by a hardlink (`cp -al`) | "publishes once, and a fresh checkout COPIES the entry" |
| rename-race fallback removed | "drops its own copy when a concurrent run renamed" |
| stand-in exclusion removed | "packs the tree into the pinned-build directories" |
| eviction `keep` off by one | "keeps the current entry and the most recently used others" |

## Gates (local, at `098d4cb`)

- `pnpm exec vitest run` over every test that names the script (`objectstack-pin`, `bump-objectstack`, `check-lockfile-dedupe`, `render-budget-comment`): 4 files, 104 tests passed, exit 0.
- `pnpm run type-check:scripts`: exit 0. `--listFilesOnly` shows both changed files in the program.
- `eslint` on the two changed scripts: exit 0.
- `check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test`: NOT GOVERNED.
- `check-changeset-presence.mjs`: no changeset owed. This matches objectui#13031, which also changed only tooling and added none.
- `check:new-line-citations`: 0 new. `check:test-path-roots`: OK. `check:pre-install-import-graph`: OK (Node builtins only). `docs:check-links`: valid.
- The full `pnpm test` farm and repo-wide lint belong to CI.

## Acceptance notes

- AGENTS.md section 9 (dependencies and lockfile) still reads true: a cold build is heavy, and removing `node_modules` means re-running setup, which is now fast. It does not name the store. The file is governed and defers the mechanism to the script header, so it is not touched here.
- Diff size: 266 changed lines (253 added, 13 removed), slightly over the ~250-line budget for this card.
